correctness.rationale: The center is trivial by fixed-point-freeness, hence so is the hypercenter. Frobenius complements partition the outside elements. For an outside target y, the map delta_y(a)=[a,y] is an injective endomorphism of the finite abelian kernel and therefore an automorphism; thus an iterated Engel commutator ending in y vanishes only when its first kernel commutator is already trivial. For a kernel target, every outside-to-kernel arc has exact depth two because the first commutator is a nontrivial kernel element and the kernel is abelian. The cyclic complement makes each complement block abelian, and fixed-point-freeness identifies the outside centralizer with the unique complement block. These facts prove all arcs and nonarcs, the strong components, the degree formulas, and the equality with the 2-Engel graph. Six brute-force semidirect-product checks independently reproduce the result.

The 2024 co-Engel paper computes special families including dihedral groups and nonabelian groups of order pq, but the inspected full text does not state the all-abelian-kernel/all-cyclic-complement directed decomposition, the exact strong-component count, or the equality with the 2-Engel graph. value.rationale: Frobenius groups are the principal soluble obstruction in the 2022 strong-connectivity theorem, so determining their component structure is directly motivated by the literature rather than by an arbitrary finite example. For a broad natural family the result replaces a qualitative nonconnectivity statement by the entire directed graph, exact Engel depths, strong-component condensation, degree data, and a closed arc count. It also extends the later prime-prime and ordinary-dihedral co-Engel patterns to arbitrary finite abelian Frobenius kernels with cyclic complement.
